title.narrative: Provision of integrated life-saving health services to the most vulnerable communities in under-served and hard-to-reach rural areas in Beletweyne

description.narrative: ltpgtThe reprioritization of the 2025 Somalia Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan (HNRP) focuses on 32 priority districts with Beletweyne, Bu’aale, Dinsoor and Qansax Dheere, experiencing significant deterioration in humanitarian conditions compared to 2024. These districts face a sharp rise in humanitarian needs due to climatic shocks, conflict, and displacement, and are projected to experience severe dry conditions. Save the Children, through this project, proposes to deploy or support two health centers, seven primary health unit (PHU) plus complemented by outreach services within catchment population. These resources will provide essential, life-saving health and protection services to communities affected by crises in Beledweyne district, which is among the four reprioritized districts for the allocation strategy. Provision of life-saving primary health care services aligns with the national essential package of health services (EPHS) framework such as clinical care, child health care, immunization, communicable disease treatment, sexual and reproductive health (antenatal care, post-natal care, safe deliveries and dignity kits for pregnant women as well as newborn care), emergency treatment and outbreak response including AWD/Cholera. The project targets vulnerable groups among the affected communities with a focus on children and pregnant women in newly established sites for displaced people, and residents in rural and hard to reach areas in Beledweyne. The project will establish and strengthen formal referral pathways for survivors of GBV and other child protection concerns, linking health services directly with specialized case management. This includes referrals for malnourished children, pregnant women with complication, and access to Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) linkages. Prevention and response to outbreaks of diseases will be achieved through active surveillance, social mobilization, education and advocacy using integrated community-based volunteers, early detection, and early treatment of infected patients. The project is designed to tackle gender-related challenges by scrutinizing project data to pinpoint disparities, implement interventions sensitive to gender issues, and guarantee the involvement and empowerment of women. The project will specifically focus on People Living with Disabilities, women, and minority groups to guarantee their access to services. The effectiveness of this focus will be evaluated through the collection of data disaggregated by disability, gender, and age at all stages. In line with the Centrality of Protection, measures will be put in place to ensure safe and dignified access to services, actively mitigating protection risks for all beneficiaries.ltbrgtTo ensure protection is central to this health response, SC will implement a robust CP/GBV mainstreaming strategy. Health workers will be trained on identifying signs of abuse, neglect, and exploitation, and utilizing safe, confidential referral protocols for child protection and GBV cases. This will strengthen the formal referral pathway between health facilities and specialized protection services, ensuring children and women at risk receive comprehensive support. Furthermore, regular coordination meetings between health and protection teams will ensure seamless information sharing and case follow-up. Proactive prevention will be prioritized through targeted community outreach and awareness-raising sessions on critical child protection issues. The project will also distribute dignity kits which include not only essential hygiene items but also discreet information on available GBV support services. These integrated activities ensure that our life-saving health services also function as a critical protective safety net for the most vulnerable.The project is estimated to directly reach 64,211 (14,152 men, 20,476 women 14,805 boys 14,778 girls) vulnerable people with lifesaving primary health care servicesltbrgtlt/pgt
